relations.evidence: If you are using the Query Workbench, you don't need to specify the transaction ID, as long as the statement is part of a multi-statement request. When you start a transaction within a multi-statement request, all statements within the request are assumed to be part of the same transaction until you rollback or commit the transaction.

relations.evidence: Similarly, if you are using the cbq shell, you don't need to specify the transaction ID. Once you have started a transaction, all statements within the cbq shell session are assumed to be part of the same transaction until you rollback or commit the transaction.

notable_absence.finding: No version, edition, deprecation or access-control statement, identical to the Capella twin's finding. Also absent: any statement of what happens if TO SAVEPOINT names a savepoint that does not exist, and any statement of whether savepoints later than the target are discarded on a partial rollback (the worked example demonstrates rolling back to s2 while s1 still exists, but the prose never says so). Both are behaviours a reader would need, and both are missing on both products.

cross_component_finding: The cbq-shell failure-recovery note ('you must use the `ROLLBACK TRANSACTION` statement to remove the transaction context and reset the transaction ID') is the only place in the batch where transaction state is described as living in a CLIENT session rather than on the server. It pairs with the implicitlySetsParameter edges: precisely because cbq infers txid from session state, it is cbq that can be left holding stale state after a failure. The Query REST API, which requires txid explicitly, has no equivalent cleanup obligation stated anywhere - a coherent design consequence that the docs never spell out, and a good candidate for the ontology to express (surface infers state -> surface needs explicit teardown).
cross_product_finding: Semantically identical to the Capella twin; all divergence is the batch-wide access-surface paragraph block (Server-only: REST API txid requirement, Query Workbench multi-statement-request inference, cbq inference plus the cbq 2.0 footnote) plus the worked example being re-rendered from cbq> transcripts into the Query Workbench multi-statement _sequence_num/_sequence_query/_sequence_result response shape. Notably the cbq-specific failure-recovery NOTE is present on BOTH products verbatim, on both this page and commit-transaction.md - so cbq operational guidance is shared content even where the surrounding surface documentation is not.
version_finding: Nothing beyond the batch-wide availableSince version:cbq-2-0. Worth stating as a negative result for the wave: ROLLBACK TRANSACTION's syntax carries an optional clause and three interchangeable optional keywords - exactly the shape where renamedFrom / mustUseInsteadWhen / deprecatedIn would normally have evidence - and the docs attach no version history to any of them. Across all six pages of this batch there are zero renamed options, zero superseded syntax forms and zero 'use X instead' statements, so renamedFrom and deprecatedIn get no evidence at all from the most-diverged corner of the n1ql tree.
